item.title: Doublethinking disinfo in Lithuania
item.description:
Intro

💼 Not a job: a paragraph before the jobs section.

 

INVESTIGATIVE JOURNALISM TECH | JOURNALISM | WATCHDOGGING GOVERNMENT | FIGHT DISINFORMATION | MEDIA | THE TECH | WATCHDOGGING AND TRANSPARENCY | ADVOCACY TECH | CORRUPTION | ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE | HUMAN RIGHTS:
🚀 Cuestión Pública CLAIM

The Colombian investigative outlet Cuestión Pública has gone on the attack against disinformation by getting verified info (from work already done) into trending conversations.

Its AI tool, Odín, draws on a database of 4,200+ Colombian politicians and companies and cross-checks against years of the outlet's own investigations. So when someone hits the headlines, it surfaces previous findings and drafts a sourced thread.

"As an investigative outlet, we spend a lot of time doing investigations and miss the news agenda," said founder Claudia Báez.

It's a kind of fact-reminding rather than fact-checking, and because it doesn't require new work, it can be a whole lot more responsive. Crucially, because it only draws from the outlet's own verified data, and not the open internet, it amplifies real reporting and avoids hallucinations.

It would be great to see this sort of practice picked up elsewhere.

item.title: The view from the window
item.description:
Intro

💼 Not a job: a paragraph before the jobs section.

 

New in ACCELERATORS | ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) | COURSES | GET FUNDING | POLICY:
🚀 AI Civic Action Accelerator CLAIM

Aspen Policy Academy has opened applications for its AI Civic Action Accelerator. It's a free six-session course for folks with a civic AI policy idea and no clear path to getting it heard. 

If you have a rough proposal for improving things like public engagement, youth online safety, handling AI job displacement, etc, then they can help you scope it, map stakeholders, and build an advocacy plan. The whole thing ends (as a lot of accelerators do) with a pitch session. 

Although it leans towards qualified applicants and subject matter experts, the program’s also open to newcomers and members of the community on a mission. However, we should also note it's US-only, and if you miss more than two hours or skip the assignments, then you're on the hook for fees.

🔌 Following up from last week
Last week we opened up the Field Guide's open-source directory of 12,000+ projects to direct access through two new connections: an MCP server and a REST API. That means you can point your own tools, agents, and workflows straight at the data and pull whatever you need with ease.
For general information and how-tos, visit the new Build portal. You can also watch a recording of our recent event, where Nathan Storey explains how he used an MCP server in his own work.
